label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L=8-9), sparse and token-dependent
explanation: Almost all activation (98% of mass) is on the delimiter step, and only in long sequences: L=9 holds about 60% of the mass, L=8 about 36%, L=7 about 2%, and L<=6 never fires. A small remainder sits on the last original token (t=L-1) of L=9 sequences. It never fires during the copy phase or earlier in the original phase. Even within long-sequence delimiters it is sparse: only about 8% (L=8) to 12% (L=9) of them fire, so precision is around 0.10 while recall and mass recall are around 0.95. Which delimiters fire depends on content in a diffuse, lookup-table way. A last original token (prev_tok) of f, z, q, 1 or s gives roughly 3-5x lift, and some first tokens (j, w, e, k, g, r, b) help a little. Adding these token lists raises F1 only to about 0.4, and I found no simple rule for them. Magnitude is larger for L=9 than L=8 and larger with the favoured prev_tok letters.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: f, z, q, 1, s, b; least: w, o, k, i) and the third original token (most: v, i, o, t, k, a; least: q, f, b, 0); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=9 & t=9, L=9 & t=8.
